# Spec: merge-auto
<!-- Generated by /hefesto:hef.spec -->
<!-- Date: 2026-11-09 -->
<!-- Board item: HEF-30 (owner decision 2026-11-09; friction measurement: every PR was a human:merge form plus an approve dialog) -->

## Overview

Three cuts to the merge friction measured on the production board: (a) `orchestrate.merge_by: auto` lets the
deploy stage merge a PR into the **integration branch** with no form when every gate, CI and every
`orchestrate.merge.checks` command pass; (b) under `merge_by: lane|person` the orchestrator asks **one multi-select
form per pass** for all mergeable PRs, and one train form covers all of a train's repositories; (c)
`orchestrate.decider` names the `--by` person so the "which name records your decisions" question is never asked
when it is set.

## Context (read from the code, 2026-11-09)

- `merge_by` is read **only** by `commands/hef.orchestrate.md` (step 2, `human:merge` row and "The lane merge");
  no helper reads it. `person` is the default.
- The verify launcher blocks every passing build on `human:merge` (`hooks/session-launch.sh:418`); the deploy
  launcher re-blocks `human:merge` on a babysitter verdict `mergeable` (`:427`), `conflict` on a conflict, `ci`
  after `MAX_FIXES` on red checks.
- The lane merge already has a deterministic pipeline in `hooks/ledger-recipes.sh`: `merge_scope` pins the head
  through `gh`, `merge_checks_get` validates `orchestrate.merge.checks` (placeholders `{repo_path}`, `{base}`),
  `merge_state_step` refuses BEHIND / non-CLEAN / non-green, `merge_done` records the merge through the one
  evidence check (`merge_evidence`) and advances to `merged`.
- `.claude/project-status.json` **is a file a lane can write** (`hooks/ledger-recipes.sh:10`): config only drafts;
  trust comes from a person's decision recorded in the approvals store under `~/.cache/hefesto/approvals/`
  (`hooks/ledger-actions.sh:13`), outside every sandbox's write set.
- `ledger.sh branches` (`hooks/ledger.sh:124-129`) yields `{integration, protected, environments, final}`; the
  effective `protected` set always contains `main`, `master`, the integration branch and every environment.
- Verdicts (`ledger.sh verdict`) record gate, verdict, by, at, evidence — **no head SHA**.
- `hooks/hefesto-setup.sh` writes Claude Code settings only; it does not write the board config today.

## Decisions taken without a clarification (documented, reviewable)

- **D1 — auto needs a person's standing grant, not only config.** Because a lane can write
  `project-status.json`, `merge_by: auto` in config alone never merges. `ledger.sh merge-auto preview` prints what
  a grant would pin and its sha256: **per board repository** (an in-repo board: one, named `.`) its resolved path,
  its `origin` `owner/repo`, its integration branch (from `branches --repo`, as `merge_repo_ctx` resolves it), and
  the `orchestrate.merge.checks` list. The orchestrator shows that preview in a form; **Turn on** runs
  `ledger.sh merge-auto grant --sha <first 12 of the preview's sha256> --reviewed-by-human --by <name>` (its
  permission dialog is the signature; a sha that no longer matches the preview is refused, as `approve` refuses).
  The grant lives in the approvals store. Config `auto` without a matching grant — no grant, or any pinned value
  that changed since (a path, an origin, an integration branch, the checks) — behaves as `person`, and the
  orchestrator asks the grant form again. `ledger.sh merge-auto revoke` removes it. The pinned checks and paths are
  what `automerge` uses: an edit to the config after the grant never reaches an unsandboxed run unseen.
- **D2 — "the integration branch, never a protected or environment branch".** The PR's base must equal the
  entry's repository's `branches.integration` exactly (per repo on a multi-repo board), and the PR's `owner/repo`
  must equal that repository's pinned `origin`; the integration branch must not be `main`/`master`, not match a
  user-declared `branches.protected` glob, and must not be the final environment (with no `branches` block the
  integration branch is `main`, the final environment, so auto never applies — promotions stay human trains).
- **D3 — the gates are for the head being merged.** The verify launcher records the head it verified
  (`.pr.verified_head`); auto-merge requires the PR's current head to equal it and the latest verdict of each of
  `verify`, `review`, `quality`, `scan` (and the entry's kind gate — its `item_kind` when that is `incident` or
  `vulnerability`, as `session-launch.sh` derives it) to be `PASS`. A babysitter fix
  that moves the head, a `SKIPPED` gate (e.g. a fix-route item with no `verify` run), or a missing verdict falls
  back to `human:merge` — the ordinary form path — never to a merge.
- **D4 — the merge is a helper, not a model.** The deploy launcher calls `ledger.sh automerge <id>`, which reuses
  the lane-merge pipeline (pinned head, CLEAN + green state, the merge checks, `gh pr merge --merge
  --match-head-commit`, `merge_evidence`, advance to `merged`). No model runs `gh pr merge`.
- **D4b — under resolved `auto` there is no merge wait.** The verify launcher, when `merge-by` resolves to `auto`,
  advances the entry to `pr` and leaves it **unblocked** (the deploy stage already selects unblocked `pr` entries).
  Only a skipped auto-merge sets `human:merge`, and then the ordinary form path applies. Because the deploy
  launcher's merged-check today runs only for `human:merge` entries, under `auto` it also runs `ledger.sh automerge
  <id> --if-merged` first: a PR a person merged by hand is recorded through the same evidence path, never reported
  as `closed`.
- **D5 — the batched form respects AskUserQuestion's limits**: at most four questions × four options per form.
  A question holding two or more PRs is multi-select with one option per PR (unselected = Later), so up to 16
  PRs per form; a question holding a single PR has that PR and **Later** (two options — a one-option question is
  rejected). More than 16 → the rest in the next pass ("then N more" in the brief).
- **D7 — a train is one form.** `request --train` already drafts one action for every repo; the gap is the
  irreversible confirmation, today "one option per irreversible step" — one per repo for a train, which overflows
  four options past three repos and reads as a question per repo. For a train it becomes one question: "Yes, merge
  all N promotions (<repos>)" / "No".
- **D6 — the decider is a label, not proof** (as today): setup writes `orchestrate.decider` from
  `git config user.name` only when the key is absent and the name is non-empty; the permission dialog stays the proof.

## User Scenarios

### US1: A green PR into the integration branch merges itself [P1]
- **Given** `orchestrate.merge_by: auto`, a standing grant for integration branch `dev`, `branches` `{integration:
  dev, environments: [dev, stg, main]}`, entry HEF-7 at phase `pr` whose PR targets `dev`, latest verdicts verify /
  review / quality / scan all `PASS` at head H, the PR's head still H, CLEAN, checks green, every merge check exits 0
- **When** the deploy stage runs for HEF-7 (worker or interactive lane)
- **Then** `ledger.sh automerge HEF-7` merges with a merge commit pinned to H, the entry is `merged` with the merge
  SHA stamped, an event `{kind: "auto-merged", by: "ledger"}` is recorded, no `human:merge` block is ever set, and
  the orchestrator brief lists it under "Done since the last pass" as `✓ HEF-7 · auto-merged PR #N into dev (<sha>)`
- **And** between verify and the merge, HEF-7 sits at `pr` unblocked: the orchestrator asks no form for it, and
  the brief shows `▷ HEF-7 · awaiting auto-merge (PR #N)`
- **Edge**: the babysitter pushed a fix after verify (head H2 ≠ H) → no merge; HEF-7 is blocked `human:merge` (the
  form path), and the brief says why ("head moved since verify")
- **Edge**: a person merged the PR by hand before the deploy pass → `automerge --if-merged` records it through the
  merge evidence and advances to `merged`; it is never reported as `closed`
- **Error**: `gh pr merge` fails or `merge_evidence` finds no merge → the entry stays `pr`, blocked `ci` with the
  helper's stderr as reason; nothing is recorded as merged
- **Must NOT**: merge without the grant; merge when config says `lane`/`person`; run `gh pr merge` from a model

### US2: An environment or protected target never auto-merges [P1]
- **Given** the US1 setup, but the PR's base is `stg` (an environment) — or `main`, or a branch matching
  `branches.protected`, or there is no `branches` block
- **When** the deploy stage runs
- **Then** the entry is blocked `human:merge` exactly as today; `gh pr merge` is never invoked
- **Edge**: the integration branch, a repo path, an origin or the checks changed in config after the grant → the
  grant does not match; behaves as `person`, and the orchestrator asks the grant form again
- **Edge**: the PR's `owner/repo` is not the entry repository's pinned `origin` → skipped, `human:merge`
- **Error**: `ledger.sh branches` fails (malformed config) → `automerge` refuses naming it; the entry blocks
  `human:merge`, never merges

### US3: A failing merge check blocks ci [P1]
- **Given** the US1 setup but one `orchestrate.merge.checks` command exits non-zero
- **When** `automerge` runs
- **Then** no merge; the entry is blocked `ci` with the failing command and its last output line as reason; the
  merge command never runs
- **Edge**: the PR is BEHIND or CONFLICTING → blocked `conflict` (the babysitter path, as today), not `ci`
- **Error**: checks still pending → nothing recorded, the entry stays at `pr` unblocked for the next deploy pass

### US4: One merge form per pass [P1]
- **Given** `merge_by: lane` (or `person`) and three entries blocked `human:merge`
- **When** the orchestrator runs step 2
- **Then** it asks **one** form with one multi-select question listing every mergeable PR (link, full head SHA,
  the four verdicts); each selected PR → under `lane`, the `approve` of its drafted merge action (and a ring of
  the deployer); under `person`, it is recorded as "I merged it" for the next deploy pass; unselected = Later
- **Edge**: one mergeable PR → the question has the PR and "Later" (two options; a one-option question is rejected)
- **Edge**: more than 16 → the first 16 (oldest `since` first); the rest in the next pass, "(then N more)" in the brief
- **Must NOT**: ask one form per PR; approve a PR the person did not select

### US5: One train form for all its repositories [P2]
- **Given** a train `release` over repos `api`, `web`, each with an open promotion PR
- **When** the person asks to promote the train
- **Then** one `request --train` action covers every repo, and one form approves it: the Approve question plus
  ONE irreversible question "Yes, merge all N promotions (<repos>)" / "No" — never one question or form per repository
- **Edge**: a train of five repos still fits one form (two questions, two options each)

### US6: The decider is remembered [P1]
- **Given** `orchestrate.decider: "Ana"` in the board config
- **When** the orchestrator needs `--by` for any decision
- **Then** it uses `"Ana"` and never asks "which name records your decisions"
- **Edge**: the key is absent → it asks once per session as today (`git config user.name` first)
- **Edge**: setup runs, `git config user.name` is "Ana", the key is absent → setup writes `orchestrate.decider: "Ana"`;
  the key present → left unchanged; the name empty → nothing written, setup says so
- **Error**: the value is not a non-empty single-line string → ignored with a warning; the orchestrator asks

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-001 | `orchestrate.merge_by` accepts `person` (default), `lane`, `auto`; any other value is refused naming it by `ledger.sh merge-by`, and every caller treats that refusal as an error (never as `person`) | P1 | US1 |
| FR-002 | `ledger.sh merge-auto preview` prints, per board repo, its path, `origin` owner/repo and integration branch, plus the merge checks, and the sha256 of all of it; `merge-auto grant --sha <12> --reviewed-by-human --by <name>` records it in the approvals store when the sha matches; `merge-auto revoke` removes it; `merge-auto show` prints it (exit 1 without one); grant/revoke are refused from a launched worker and from a lane session that is not the orchestrator | P1 | US1, US2 |
| FR-003 | `ledger.sh merge-by` resolves `auto` only when a grant exists and every pinned value equals the current one (each repo's path, origin, integration branch; the checks); otherwise it prints `person` and the mismatch on stderr | P1 | US1, US2 |
| FR-004 | The verify launcher records `.pr.verified_head` (the worktree's HEAD it verified) when it transcribes the verdicts; under resolved `auto` it advances to `pr` without blocking `human:merge` | P1 | US1 |
| FR-005 | `ledger.sh automerge <id>` merges only when: FR-003 holds; the entry is at `pr`; the PR's owner/repo equals the entry repo's pinned origin; the PR base equals that repo's pinned integration branch, which is not `main`/`master`, not a declared protected glob, not the final environment; the latest verdict of verify, review, quality, scan (and the kind gate, if any) is `PASS`; the PR head equals `.pr.verified_head`; `pr-watch.sh state` is CLEAN/HAS_HOOKS with checks `pass`; every pinned merge check exits 0 | P1 | US1, US2, US3 |
| FR-006 | `automerge` merges with `gh pr merge <n> -R <repo> --merge --match-head-commit <verified head>`, records the merge through `merge_evidence`, stamps the merge SHA, adds an `auto-merged` event and advances to `merged` (exit 0) | P1 | US1 |
| FR-007 | A precondition of FR-005 that does not hold, other than those in FR-008/FR-009, blocks `human:merge`, records the reason as an `auto-merge-skipped` event and exits 2; it never merges | P1 | US1, US2 |
| FR-008 | A failing merge check (or one that times out), a check refused by `cmd_ok` or `check_path_plain`, or a failing merge/evidence step (GitHub refusing a moved head) blocks `ci` with the command and its reason and exits 3 | P1 | US3 |
| FR-009 | BEHIND or CONFLICTING blocks `conflict` (exit 3); checks pending records nothing (exit 4) | P1 | US3 |
| FR-010 | The deploy launcher, when `merge-by` resolves to `auto`: runs `automerge <id> --if-merged` first (a PR merged by hand is recorded, exit 0, nothing launched); on a babysitter verdict `mergeable` calls `automerge <id>` instead of blocking `human:merge`; a `merge-by` failure stops the launch with its message (worker and `--finish` paths alike) | P1 | US1 |
| FR-011 | The orchestrator brief reports each auto-merge since the last pass, each entry awaiting auto-merge, and the reason of every skipped auto-merge | P2 | US1 |
| FR-012 | `hef.orchestrate.md`: all `human:merge` entries go in one form per pass (D5: multi-select per up-to-four PRs, a single-PR question gets Later, ≤16, oldest first; link, full head SHA, verdicts); under resolved `auto` nothing is asked for unblocked `pr` entries; config `auto` without a matching grant → one grant form showing `merge-auto preview` | P1 | US1, US4 |
| FR-013 | `hef.orchestrate.md:208-209`: a train's irreversible confirmation is one question ("Yes, merge all N promotions (<repos>)" / "No"), so a train is one form whatever its length | P2 | US5 |
| FR-014 | `hef.orchestrate.md`: `orchestrate.decider`, when a non-empty single-line string, is the `--by` name and the name question is not asked | P1 | US6 |
| FR-015 | `hefesto-setup.sh` writes `orchestrate.decider` from `git config user.name` when the key is absent and the name non-empty; never overwrites; `--print` shows it; `--remove` leaves it; setup's `permissions.ask` gains `ledger.sh merge-auto grant*` and `revoke*` | P2 | US6 |
| FR-016 | Docs (`docs/quickstart.md`, `docs/quickstart.pt-BR.md`, `docs/install.md`, `docs/architecture.md`) and `CHANGELOG.md` describe `auto`, the grant, the batched form and `decider` | P2 | all |

### Negative requirements

| ID | Must NOT happen | Scenario |
|----|-----------------|----------|
| NR-001 | No merge into an environment, `main`/`master`, or a declared protected branch by `automerge` — ever | US2 |
| NR-002 | No model (orchestrator, lane, worker) runs `gh pr merge` for `auto`; only `ledger.sh automerge` does | US1 |
| NR-003 | Config alone (no grant) never enables a merge | US1 |
| NR-004 | No merge at a head the gates did not see | US1 |
| NR-005 | No merge check runs that the person did not see at grant time (each validated by the action scope's `cmd_ok`, run as argv, never through a shell) | US3 |

## Success Criteria

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | A PR with four PASS gates at its head, into the granted integration branch, merges with no block | `tests/smoke-merge.sh` with FakeGhPr: `gh pr merge … --match-head-commit` in the log, entry `merged`, no `human:merge` |
| SC-002 | The same PR against an environment branch blocks `human:merge`, no `gh pr merge` call | smoke, same fixture |
| SC-003 | A failing merge check blocks `ci`, no `gh pr merge` call | smoke |
| SC-004 | Without the grant, or with a moved head, or a non-PASS gate → `human:merge`, no merge | smoke |
| SC-005 | `orchestrate.decider` is read from config; setup writes it only when absent | smoke (setup `--print` on a fixture) + structural grep on `hef.orchestrate.md` |
| SC-006 | The orchestrator text asks one form per pass for merges and one per train | structural smoke on `hef.orchestrate.md` |
| SC-008 | Security paths: grant refused with `HEFESTO_WORKER=1` and from a non-orchestrator lane; a grant whose sha does not match the preview refused; a tampered store check that fails `cmd_ok` refused before anything runs; a `{repo_path}` with a space refused; `gh pr merge` refused by the fake (moved head) → `ci`, nothing recorded; a PR from another origin → `human:merge`; an invalid `merge_by` stops the deploy launch | `tests/smoke-automerge.sh`, one assertion each on the fake's log and the entry |
| SC-009 | Under resolved `auto` a verified entry is at `pr` unblocked; a PR merged by hand is recorded by `--if-merged`, not `closed` | smoke |
| SC-007 | Each guard above is mutation-tested: removing it turns the suite red | mutation run recorded in the task evidence (constitution 3) |

## Clarifications
_None — D1–D6 above record the decisions taken from the code._
